title: "A Comeback after 4 years to the blues" | Ravichandran Ashwin press conference | IND vs SCO Match
quote_text:
Ravichandran Ashwin came to the pre-match press conference of the Indian team on Thursday. The media broadly had two issues to ask him. First- his bowling against Afghanistan, second- preparation for the match against Scotland on Friday. The interesting thing is that in the entire press conference, the very first issue dominated. The bottom line of every question was that after four years, when he has come back in quick cricket, what would he like to say? Actually, it was very common discussion in the dressing room sources regarding R Ashwin that he is no longer the first choice of captain Virat Kohli and coach Ravi Shastri. It is also said that the current mentor of the Indian team, Mahendra Singh Dhoni also no longer likes Ashwin as before.

If we go to the bottom of it, maybe some other story will come out, but it is true that even after consistent good performance, R Ashwin was not able to get a place in the playing-11 in quick cricket. Due to the good performance of Yuzvendra Chahal and Kuldeep Yadav, they also had to wait for a long time. Later Ravindra Jadeja also returned to the team but it was written to wait for Ashwin’s luck. Also selected in the team of T20 World Cup 2021, Virat Kohli gave priority to Varun Chakraborty in the important match against Pakistan and New Zealand. However, India had to lose both the matches by a huge margin.

Initiating the press conference, Ashwin said that when he was selected in the T20 World Cup squad, it was a special moment for him. Ashwin said- “Life is like a ‘circle’. For some this ‘circle’ is small for some it is big. I learned to be restrained in bad times. I had to prove my usefulness to someone else rather than myself. I kept working hard and always prepared that wherever you put three wickets, I will bowl.

Ashwin wanted to say that good and bad times come to everyone in life. He also gave the example of Shane Warne and Sachin Tendulkar regarding success. Ashwin also answered the question of success against Afghanistan and being economical as a spinner versus taking wickets. 

“I have been playing in this format since 2007-08. This game changes very fast. There are always ‘dot balls’ behind getting a wicket which puts pressure on the batsman. During this process I also think about the team ‘interest’. For me every match is a 24-ball event, every time I want to win. The success in the match against Afghanistan is a ‘special night’ for me."

Just after this R Ashwin was thrown out of cricket immediately. Ashwin was almost constant in the Test team. During this, Ashwin’s role was in whatever historic victory India recorded. He was the hero of the glorious victory in Australia. But he was not being ‘considered’ in quick cricket. That place was taken by the pair of Kuldeep and Chahal. But now that pair has also broken up. Ashwin is back. He has once again got a place in the playing 11 along with Jadeja. So is R Ashwin’s cricket circle complete, in R Ashwin’s language the ‘circle’ is never complete. There are stops in it.
